llm.summary: The skill is coherent for Outlit customer intelligence, but its setup instructions include an unverified remote installer piped directly into Bash.

dimensions.detail: The requested environment access is broad but expected for a customer-data integration: it uses Outlit API keys, OAuth/MCP, CLI commands, SQL reads, and integration setup flows for workspace customer data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The CLI setup section documents `curl -fsSL https://outlit.ai/install.sh | bash`, which executes mutable remote code without a review or integrity-verification step, even though node and Homebrew alternatives are also provided.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifact repeatedly scopes write operations to explicit user requests, requires extra care for irreversible customer merges, and warns not to bypass agent or permission boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor-like persistence is shown, but the skill may install or configure the Outlit CLI/skill and can use stored credentials; destructive merge execution is explicitly permissioned and not the default.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's customer intelligence, SQL analytics, integration setup, access management, and merge workflows match its stated Outlit purpose, including clear evidence-gathering and read-only SQL rules.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use the package-manager install options where possible, such as npm or Homebrew, and avoid running the curl-to-bash installer unless you trust the publisher and understand it will execute remote code on your machine. Also review Outlit API key grants carefully because the skill can access sensitive customer data and, with explicit permissions, change access, settings, integrations, and customer merges.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: Installing the Outlit CLI is purpose-aligned, but the documented pipe-to-shell installer is a real supply-chain concern because it lacks version pinning or checksum/signature verification.
[TM2] expected: This is the same install-path concern as SC2: the shell pipeline is disclosed but removes a user review step before execution.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited 'Do not ask the user' text is credential-safety guidance telling agents not to collect provider secrets in chat; surrounding instructions require explicit user requests for workspace writes and explicit authorization for merges.
[T03] expected: The static finding is supported by the CLI setup command; it warrants Review because the installer can execute changing remote content, not because the rest of the skill is deceptive.
